title: cymba mobile and laptop companion-app concept v2 — active deep-work session
status: Proposed app design for review; not integrated into the landing page
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Edit target: the attached paired laptop and phone cymba app mockup.
Request: Redesign BOTH app screens completely to create a significantly more capable, useful and visually compelling companion app for demanding cognitive work. Preserve the photorealistic laptop and phone hardware, device placement, readable near-front perspective, pure white studio background, soft contact shadows, and entire devices in frame. Screen UI is the only area to redesign. Produce the highest practical resolution, with sharp readable typography.

Design: A sophisticated dark graphite native-app workspace, like expertly crafted premium productivity software. Near-black #131419 app background, subtly differentiated charcoal #1c1e25 panels, thin quiet borders, off-white crisp typography, muted grey secondary labels, restrained lavender #aa91ef for brain signals and selected states, teal #6cbcb7 for pulse. Refined visual hierarchy, ample breathing room within a purposeful dashboard, elegant small functional icons. No neon cyberpunk, decorative brain pictures, glowing spheres, huge empty buttons, rainbow charts, fake productivity or cognition scores. Useful information takes priority. Broad composed sections, not a wall of identical metric cards.

LAPTOP UI:
A slim left sidebar with white lowercase "cymba" wordmark at the top; navigation "Session" (selected in subtle violet tint), "History", "Insights", "Settings". At the bottom a discreet connected-device status "Earbuds connected".
Main top bar: large heading "Deep work", a small "Demo data" chip at the far right.
Main content has a generous primary session panel on the left and a narrower live-signals panel on the right. BELOW both is a compact weekly history band.

Primary session panel:
Small label "WORKING ON"
Clear task title "Design the next iteration"
A prominent beautifully typeset elapsed timer "24:18", with small label "Session time".
An understated small teal status dot with text "Personalised timing active".
A compact lavender primary button "Pause", with a quieter secondary "End session". Buttons are appropriately sized controls, not full-width empty slabs.
Lower part of this panel: a meaningful visual timeline heading "This session". A horizontal time ruler with tick labels "0", "10", "20", "Now". Thin lavender event bars mark actual illustrative stimulation intervals, against a muted background. Under it a tiny legend "Stimulation" and "Sensing". Use a thin activity line and event marks to make the adaptive timing feel understandable, not just decorative.
A discreet explanation below the timeline: "Timing adapts to your brain and pulse signals."
At the bottom, a compact outlined input with a small plus icon and label "Park a thought". This is a distraction-capture action, not a prominent marketing feature.

Live-signals panel:
Heading "Live signals", small status "Good contact".
Two clearly separated compact graphs: "Brain activity" in lavender, and "Pulse" in teal. Brain activity is a fine irregular EEG-like oscillation over a faint grid, no invented cognitive labels or scores. Pulse MUST be an optical PPG waveform, NOT an ECG: smooth repeated arterial hills with rounded peak and small dicrotic notch on the downward slope, no tall needle-like spikes or deep negative troughs. No clinical interpretation or performance percentages.
Small footer status "Signals guiding session timing".

Bottom history band:
Left portion heading "This week", large "6h 20m" with label "Session time", and a tasteful small bar chart with seven quiet lavender bars labelled "M T W T F S S", bars vary naturally.
Right portion heading "Pick up where you left off", two concise recent-session rows with subtle separators:
"System design" / "38 min" and smaller note "Next: compare two approaches"
"Reading & research" / "26 min" and smaller note "Next: finish the final section"
This should feel genuinely useful and thoughtfully organised, not cluttered with tiny dummy text. Keep phone overlap away from crucial controls and main heading.

PHONE UI:
Same coherent dark palette, typography and icon system, designed natively for mobile rather than a shrunken desktop. Lowercase white "cymba" at the top, small subtle "Demo" chip.
Heading "Deep work".
Task text "Design the next iteration".
Large clear "24:18" with small "Session time" beneath it.
Small teal status dot and "Personalised timing active".
One compact, beautifully composed live-session panel with a restrained lavender brain waveform, correct rounded teal PPG waveform, labels "Brain activity" and "Pulse", and a short thin stimulation event strip labelled "This session".
One lavender "Pause" button and a quiet "End" control side by side.
A small functional "Park a thought" field below.
Three clean bottom navigation icons with labels "Session", "History", "Settings"; Session highlighted.
Keep everything inside the screen, with good margins and finger-sized controls. No extra hamburger button that duplicates bottom navigation.

Constraints: Exact supplied text, legible hierarchy, no gibberish filler. Illustrative APP CONCEPT using demo data and proposed software features. No claims of demonstrated cognitive improvement, focus accuracy, personalised dose recommendations, medical readings, fixed prescribed session lengths, Bluetooth, battery or platform compatibility. No OS or hardware manufacturer logos. Preserve realistic clean hardware and white surrounding background, make the screens feel like a product someone would actually want to use.
proposedFeatures: Work intention and elapsed session timer
Brain and pulse signals with contact status
notes: Illustrative demo signals and example session history; concept features do not establish a finished app, validated cognitive outcomes, or confirmed platform compatibility.
